title: Curbing Scam Calls Made From +65 Prefix Phone Numbers
what_it_is: Curbing Scam Calls Made From +65 Prefix Phone Numbers

sections.label: +65 prefix anti-scam efforts
sections.summary: The +65 prefix alerts the public to overseas calls, and IMDA works with telcos to block suspected scam calls and teaches seniors cyber safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The +65 prefix which we implemented with telecommunication companies (telcos) in April last year helps to alert the public that these are calls coming from overseas and that the public should not pick up such calls if they are not expecting anyone calling from overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: This is part of our broader anti-scam efforts, including the expeditious blocking of known numbers used to perpetuate scams or those attempting to spoof the numbers of Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: IMDA will continue to work with telcos on solutions that telcos can deploy within their networks to enhance their ability to detect and block suspected scam calls, while ensuring that genuine calls continue to be efficiently connected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: In this spirit, IMDA teaches seniors cyber safety tips such as how to identify spoofed scam calls via its Seniors Go Digital programme.

sections.label: Police grassroots scam alerts
sections.summary: The Police work with Residents' Committees and grassroots volunteers to spread scam alerts to residents, including seniors, via WhatsApp and community events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: For instance, the Police work with Residents’ Committees and grassroots volunteers to spread scam alerts to residents, including senior citizens, via WhatsApp and community events like block parties, roadshows, festive events and Community Safety and Security Programmes.

sections.label: Blocking +65 calls problem
sections.summary: Blocking the source of +65 calls is complicated because legitimate calls, such as Singaporeans roaming overseas calling home, also use the +65 prefix.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, the first question is whether MCI and MHA would look into blocking the source of these +65 calls in a more concerted way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is unfortunately a problem in that there are also legitimate calls that will end up using the +65 prefix, for example, Singaporeans who are roaming overseas and calling back home.

sections.label: Public vigilance against scams
sections.summary: The main prevention is the vigilance of the public and awareness of what a scam might look like and what scammers may be trying to get away with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The main prevention is going to be the vigilance of the public, the awareness of what a scam might look like, what they may be trying to get away with.
